author: reek
body: Application data over an AUTHENTICATED DTLS 1.3 handshake, end to end, with no network. The handshake is the authenticated loopback's; what this adds is the two rungs above it -- the server flight and both Finished messages protected at the handshake epoch (2), and then application data at epoch 3 under the application traffic keys.

author: reek
body: The record layer is oracle-validated (codex/test/dtls-record checks dtls-seal / dtls-open against an independent implementation); the key schedule is the generic TLS 1.3 one the RFC 8448 vectors gate. What this test cannot prove is interop, because no third-party DTLS peer is in the loop -- so the negative control is the tamper: a flipped ciphertext byte must yield NO plaintext, or the AEAD is decoration.

author: reek
body: The handshake shuttles datagrams between the two endpoints exactly as the authenticated loopback does; d-sh is the plaintext ServerHello and d-cert/d-cv/d-fin are the epoch-2 protected server flight. After both sides are done, a payload goes each way at epoch 3, and a tampered copy of the client's record is refused.
